title: Market Day
sub: A small game about why people buy. You mind a stall at a hill market for a day, set the prices, choose what the chalkboard says, and five villagers decide.
description: Market Day: a small browser game by Riya Dutta. Set the prices, pick the sign, and learn why each villager buys or walks away.
facts: A game in the browser, nothing to download
Six price tags and a chalkboard sign, with one chance to change the sign at lunch
The idea, the villagers, the drawing and the rules
One HTML file: every tree, stall and villager drawn in SVG

hero.alt: Riya waving beside her market stall of honey jars, apples, a woollen cap and a shawl, with a chalkboard that says Fresh this morning

sections.title: Price it, sign it, open up.
sections.note: Tap Set prices to change the six price tags, then tap the chalkboard to choose what it says. Open the stall, and change the sign once at lunch. At dusk, the ledger shows who bought, why, and how much more they would have paid. The best possible day takes ₹1,240.

items.t: Most of marketing is a nudge, not a price cut. Here you can watch five of them work on five shoppers, one at a time.
Every villager has a limit, and the right nudge stretches it. The ledger shows each reason and each limit, so the next day you can price a little smarter.

tiles.d: Pip the goat pays more for the medium honey when the big jar costs twice as much: the decoy. Kiko the yak pays more for a cap when the shawl beside it is pricey: the anchor.
Juno the monal pays up to ₹150 for apples if stock looks short. Nell the pika pays ₹120, but only once a crowd has bought. Price the apples for one, and you may lose the other.
Wren the red panda wants to know where it was made. Tell her it is local, and keep the small jar at ₹200 or less.

paras: The rest of this site is work for clients. The Lab is for things I make because I want them to exist. This one turns the ideas I use every day into a morning at a hill market. A perfect day is possible, but it takes the right prices, and the right sign at the right time.
